topics.topic: Describe the histological structure of ureter
topics.generatedNotes:
**Overview of Ureteric Histology** The *ureters* are specialized tubular structures that transport *urine* from the *kidneys* to the *urinary bladder*. The wall of the *ureter* is organized into three primary histological coats: the *mucosa*, the *muscularis*, and the *adventitia*. **The Mucosal Layer** - The *mucosa* is the innermost lining of the *ureter*. - In an empty state, the *mucosa* presents with numerous *folds*, which give the *lumen* a characteristic *star-shaped* appearance when viewed in *transverse sections*. - These *mucosal folds* are not permanent; they flatten and disappear when the *ureter* becomes distended with *urine*. - The *epithelial lining* is classified as *transitional epithelium*, which is typically composed of *3 to 5 layers* of cells. - Supporting the *epithelium* is the *lamina propria*, a layer notably rich in *collagenous fibers*. **The Muscularis Layer** - The *muscularis* is a thick layer of *smooth muscle* responsible for generating *peristaltic movements* that drive *urine* toward the *bladder*. - The orientation of the *smooth muscle* fibers changes based on the vertical position along the *ureter*. **Structural Classification of the Muscularis**
Anatomical Segment Muscle Layer Configuration
Upper Two-Thirds Composed of two layers: an *inner longitudinal layer* and an *outer circular layer*.
Lower One-Third Composed of three layers: an *inner longitudinal layer*, a *middle circular layer*, and an *outer longitudinal layer*.
**The Adventitia Layer** - The *adventitia* constitutes the outermost layer of the *ureteric wall*. - It is formed by *loose fibroelastic connective tissue*. - This layer functions as a matrix for essential structures, including *blood vessels*, *lymphatic vessels*, and *nerves*. **Functional Pathway of Urine Conduction** Formation in Kidneys → Entry into Ureter → *Peristaltic Contractions* of *Muscularis* → Discharge into *Urinary Bladder*
